intro: GPT stands for Generative Pre-trained Transformer — and the Transformer is the real hero behind ChatGPT. This episode walks through the neural network pipeline: tokens → embeddings → attention → next word prediction. Use this for revision before diving deeper.

sections.heading: Neural networks & next-word prediction
sections.definition: Just like our brain decides the next word in a sentence, a neural network does the same for LLMs. Input tokens become embeddings, pass through the network, and the model predicts the most likely next word — then repeats until done.
points: Input sentence → tokens → embeddings → neural network → next word
Generated word gets added back as input — loop continues until stop token
Stopping: end-of-sequence token or other termination logic
Neural network = computational brain that powers word-by-word generation

sections.heading: GPT: Generative Pre-trained Transformer
sections.definition: GPT is not ChatGPT — all modern LLMs use GPT-style architecture. Generative = creates new text. Pre-trained = already learned from massive data. Transformer = the architecture that makes it all work.
points: Generative: produces text, doesn't retrieve from a database
Pre-trained: model already studied huge datasets before you use it
Transformer: reads entire sequences at once using attention (since 2017)
OpenAI named their assistant ChatGPT — but GPT architecture is industry standard

sections.heading: Transformer architecture
sections.definition: Before 2017, RNNs and LSTMs processed text word-by-word and missed long-range relationships. Google's 'Attention Is All You Need' paper introduced Transformers — the foundation of ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and all modern LLMs.
points: Transformer reads entire sentence/block at once — not sequentially
Introduced in 2017 by Google researchers (Vaswani et al.)
Replaced RNN/LSTM for most NLP tasks
Heart of neural network = Transformer; heart of Transformer = Attention

sections.heading: Attention & self-attention
sections.definition: Attention helps the model focus on the most relevant words in a sentence. Self-attention lets each token look at all other tokens to understand relationships — like figuring out 'it' refers to 'cat' in 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired.'
points: Attention: focus on important parts, ignore the rest
Self-attention: each word checks all other words in the same sentence
Solves long-range dependency problems that RNNs couldn't handle
Also called: Multi-Head Attention, Causal Self-Attention, Masked Attention

sections.heading: Causal & multi-head attention
sections.definition: Causal (masked) attention prevents the model from seeing future words — only past and present tokens. Multi-head attention runs several attention processes in parallel, each focusing on different relationships.
points: Masked = hide future words; Causal = past causes present
Token can see itself + all tokens before it, never after
Multi-head: parallel attention processes capture different patterns
Information flows one direction: past → present

sections.heading: Inside a Transformer layer
sections.definition: Each Transformer layer follows a pipeline: token + positional embeddings → Layer Norm → Attention → Residual connection → Layer Norm → Feed-Forward Network → output. Residual connections preserve original info while adding updates.
points: Token Embedding + Positional Embedding → input to Transformer
Layer Norm: keeps numbers stable (mean 0, variance 1) for smooth learning
Attention: tokens communicate with each other
Residual/Skip connection: output = original input + layer update
FFN: each token processes independently what it learned from attention
Linear + Softmax: convert to probability scores → pick highest as next word

sections.heading: Attention vs FFN — the division of labor
sections.definition: Attention lets tokens talk to each other (context). Feed-Forward Network lets each token think independently about what it learned. Together they form the repeating block that powers generation.
points: Attention: 'bank' finds river meaning by looking at surrounding words
FFN: each token deepens its own representation after communication
Multiple Transformer layers stack — each refines understanding further
Final step: Linear layer reshapes → Softmax gives word probabilities → pick winner
